{{Short description|Greek-Australian building scientist and academic}}{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2026}}

'''Matthaios Santamouris''' AM is a [[Greek Australians|Greek Australian]] physicist and building scientist. He is the Anita Lawrence Chair in High Performance Architecture and a Scientia Distinguished Professor at the [[University of New South Wales]] (UNSW) in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Professor Matthaios Santamouris |url=https://research.unsw.edu.au/people/professor-matthaios-santamouris |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=research.unsw.edu.au |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Professor Matthaios Santamouris |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/staff/mattheos-santamouris |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=UNSW Sites |language=en}}</ref>He previously served as a professor of physics at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens in Greece. His research focuses on urban heat, the energy performance of buildings, cooling technologies and materials, and the effects of urban climate on the built environment and human health.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-24 |title=2026 Mattheos Santamouris: Engineering and Technology Researcher – H-Index, Publications & Awards |url=https://research.com/u/mattheos-santamouris |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
He studied physics at the University of Patras, where he received a diploma in physics and a PhD in energy physics. He later pursued postgraduate studies in energy physics at the [[Grenoble Institute of Technology|Institute National Polytechnique de Grenoble]] in [[France]], earning a Diplôme d’études approfondies (DEA).<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Santamouris spent much of his academic career at the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|National and Kapodistrian University]] of Athens, where he conducted research on energy use in buildings and the relationship between the built environment and the environment.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He also served as president of the Centre for Renewable Energy Sources and Saving (CRES), Greece's national centre for renewable energy.<ref name=":1" />

In 2016, he moved to UNSW Sydney, where he became a professor in the Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture. He was appointed a Scientia Distinguished Professor in 2019 and holds the Anita Lawrence Chair in High Performance Architecture.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Matthaios Santamouris |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/staff/mattheos-santamouris |access-date=2026-10-14 |website=UNSW Sites |language=en}}</ref>He has also held visiting professorships at several universities internationally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simos |first=Andriana |date=2022-01-19 |title=Professor Mattheos Santamouris awarded $570,000 for heat mitigation project |url=https://greekherald.com.au/community/1-people-community/professor-mattheos-santamouris-from-unsw-awarded-570000-heat-mitigation-project/ |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=The Greek Herald |language=en-AU}}</ref>

== Research ==
Santamouris's research focuses on urban climate and the energy performance of buildings, particularly the causes and effects of urban overheating and the urban heat island effect. His work has examined measures for reducing urban temperatures, including reflective materials, cool roofs and pavements, green roofs, and passive and hybrid cooling systems.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2026-08-24 |title=2026 Mattheos Santamouris: Engineering and Technology Researcher – H-Index, Publications & Awards |url=https://research.com/u/mattheos-santamouris |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref> He has also investigated the effects of urban heat on building energy use and on heat-related health, with particular attention to vulnerable populations.<ref name=":4" />

Santamouris was a senior author of a 2024 study published in Nature Cities that modelled different heat-mitigation strategies for a precinct in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The study assessed 3,323 buildings and estimated that some of the measures could reduce peak summer temperatures by up to 4.5 °C.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haddad |first=Shamila |last2=Zhang |first2=Wanni |last3=Paolini |first3=Riccardo |last4=Gao |first4=Kai |last5=Altheeb |first5=Muzahim |last6=Al Mogirah |first6=Abdulrahman |last7=Bin Moammar |first7=Abdullatif |last8=Hong |first8=Tianzhen |last9=Khan |first9=Ansar |last10=Cartalis |first10=Constantinos |last11=Polydoros |first11=Anastasios |last12=Santamouris |first12=Mattheos |date=11 January 2024 |title=Quantifying the energy impact of heat mitigation technologies at the urban scale |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s44284-023-00005-5 |journal=Nature |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=62–72 |doi=10.1038/s44284-023-00005-5 |issn=2731-9997}}</ref> <ref>{{Cite web |title=Study reveals construction materials capable of cooling |url=https://greenreview.com.au/construction/study-reveals-construction-materials-capable-of-cooling-one-of-the-worlds-hottest-cities/ |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=Green Review}}</ref>He also contributed to the 2017 Cooling Western Sydney study, commissioned by Sydney Water, which examined the use of water and reflective materials as measures for reducing urban heat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sydney Water and UNSW collaborate to cool Western Sydney |url=https://www.awa.asn.au/resources/latest-news/business/partnerships/sydney-water-and-unsw-collaborate-to-cool-western-sydney |access-date=2026-10-08 |website=www.awa.asn.au |language=en-au}}</ref>

== Editorial work ==
Santamouris is one of the two editors-in-chief of ''Energy and Buildings'', published by Elsevier, alongside Jianlei Niu of the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]].<ref>https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/energy-and-buildings/about/editorial-board</ref> UNSW additionally lists him as an associate editor and editorial-board member of other peer-reviewed journals in the fields of energy, buildings and the environment.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards and honours ==
Santamouris was appointed a [[Member of the Order of Australia]] (AM) in the [[2026 King's Birthday Honours (Australia)|King's Birthday Honours]],<ref name="honours">{{Cite web |date=2026-06-07 |author1=Dimitri Kallos|author2=Maria Kampyli|author3=Michael Georgiou|title=Almost a dozen Greek Australians receive 2026 King's Birthday Honours |url=https://neoskosmos.com/en/2026/06/07/news/australia/almost-a-dozen-greek-australians-receive-2026-kings-birthday-honours/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=NEOS KOSMOS |language=en}}</ref> "for significant service to architecture, energy and environmental quality", and has been named a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher for several consecutive years.<ref name="am-honours">{{cite web |date=June 2026 |title=UNSW community recognised with King's Birthday Honours |url=https://www.unsw.edu.au/newsroom/news/2026/06/UNSW-community-recognised-with-Kings-Birthday-Honours |access-date=2 October 2026 |website=UNSW Newsroom |publisher=University of New South Wales}}</ref><ref name="gg-honours">{{cite web |date=June 2026 |title=2026 King's Birthday Honours List – Order of Australia |url=https://www.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/KB26%20-%20Honours%20List%20-%20Order%20of%20Australia.pdf |access-date=2 October 2026 |website=Governor-General of the Commonwealth of Australia}}</ref> He was also named an Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Institute of British Architects]] (RIBA).<ref name="riba">{{cite web |date=March 2026 |title=RIBA announces 27 new Honorary Fellows |url=https://www.riba.org/news/riba-announces-27-new-honorary-fellows/ |access-date=2 October 2026 |website=Royal Institute of British Architects}}</ref> His another honours include the lifetime Achievement Award from the Passive and Low Energy Architecture (PLEA) organization for his contribution to sustainable architecture and urban overheating mitigation, as well as an honorary doctorate from the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Cyprus. He is a Fellow of the [[World Academy of Art and Science]].<ref name="waas">{{cite web |date=2026 |title=New Fellows of the World Academy of Art and Science Announced 2026 |url=https://worldacademy.org/new-fellows-of-the-world-academy-of-art-and-science-announced-2026/ |access-date=2 October 2026 |website=World Academy of Art and Science}}</ref>
